pathway.title: PROG Holdings, Inc. — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: - The business profile is adequate in scale but narrow in earnings. Progressive Leasing generated 91.73% of nine-month 2026 pre-tax profit, customers of three partners produced 54.8% of 2025 revenue, and Progressive Leasing revenue fell 4.37% in the nine months while its volume grew only 1.20%, so the profit engine is shrinking even as approvals tighten. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 50; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 63; 10-K_2025-12-31_prg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 27; calculation C1; calculation C3; calculation C4

- Credit performance at the core is the swing factor for earnings. Write-offs rose to 8.3% of Progressive Leasing revenue in Q3 2026 from 7.4%, above the top of the 6% to 8% annual target range, Q3 Progressive Leasing pre-tax earnings fell 12.65%, and company adjusted EBITDA fell 9.50% from Q2 to Q3 2026, so group adjusted EBITDA has fallen in each quarter since Q1 2026, although seasonality may explain part of that. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 61; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 63; EX-99.3_2026-10-28_ex-993q32026earningssupp.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation C5; calculation C6

- Cash conversion is strong but flatters the trend. Operating cash flow was USD 386.2 million in the first nine months of 2026 on USD 13.0 million of capital expenditure, 166.13% of reported EBITDA, but the lease merchandise balance fell USD 97.7 million as the portfolio shrank and a tax refund replaced a tax payment, so conversion would fall if volume recovered or taxes normalised. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C8; calculation C9; calculation C10; calculation C11

- Leverage is low on the recourse view but rising on the reported view, and the perimeter decides the message. The company-defined ratio, which counts only the notes, is 1.53x on a house calculation, up from 1.08x at the end of 2025 because cash was spent on the acquisition, and would be 1.85x after the announced repurchase, while reported net debt to EBITDA is 2.73x at 2026-09-30 and 3.09x pro forma for the repurchase announced on 2026-10-28 because it includes the asset-backed debt and uses EBITDA before all interest. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.3_2026-10-28_ex-993q32026earningssupp.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25; calculation C19; calculation C29

- Liquidity and the maturity profile give time, but 2029 is a single refinancing event. Cash of USD 108.9 million and an undrawn USD 350.0 million revolver give USD 458.9 million against no maturities until the USD 600.0 million of notes and the revolver both fall due in November 2029, and the estimated fair value of the notes slipped to 95.18% of par from 98.69% at the end of 2025. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 41; calculation C15; calculation C16

- Financial policy is the main controllable risk. The announced USD 100.0 million accelerated repurchase will use cash and revolver borrowings, equal to 21.79% of liquidity, while the leverage covenant steps down from 3.25x in 2026 to 3.00x in 2027 and 2.50x after, on a definition that was not supplied, so covenant headroom is not established. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C15; calculation C27

- Regulatory and legal exposure is a tail risk to the core that is not yet quantified. A civil investigative demand from a state attorney general arrived in October 2026, compliance duties from the 2020 consumer protection settlement continue, and a class action targets the cash advance product, while the company estimates the range of reasonably possible loss as immaterial and cannot predict outcomes. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 43–45; Business & governance (CP-1A)

cells.text: Financial technology holding company with three reportable segments: Progressive Leasing (lease-to-own at retail partners), Purchasing Power (employer payroll-deduction purchasing, owned from 2026-01-02) and Four (buy now pay later); MoneyApp cash advances sit in Other
Three different risk profiles under one holding company; Progressive Leasing is the cash engine
Progressive Leasing 77.70%, Purchasing Power 16.88%, Four 4.90%, Other 0.52%
Revenue is diversified more than profit
Progressive Leasing USD 138.214 million of USD 150.680 million (91.73%); Purchasing Power loss USD 4.828 million; Four USD 28.432 million; Other loss USD 11.138 million
Many are near-prime or subprime on FICO score and may struggle to buy big-ticket durables; Four scores loans by internal categories A to C rather than credit ratings
Payment performance is sensitive to cost of living, fuel prices and unemployment

About 24,000 partner locations and websites in 45 states, the District of Columbia and Puerto Rico; top three partners 54.8% and top ten 77.0% of consolidated 2025 revenue (52.6% and 78.2% in 2024); two partners each above 10% of 2025 consolidated revenue
Loss or repricing of a large partner would hit volume and revenue
Customers lease for a fixed term of up to 12 months and may cancel at any time by returning the merchandise; past-due leases are written off after 120 days
Short duration means credit tightening shows in earnings within quarters

Provision for lease merchandise write-offs was 8.3% of Progressive Leasing revenue in Q3 2026 against 7.4% a year earlier and 8.0% for nine months against 7.4%; FY2025 7.5%, FY2024 7.5% and FY2023 6.7% of lease revenues; annual target range 6% to 8%
Q3 2026 is above the top of the target range; the bases are revenue and lease revenues, which are almost equal

Corporate debt is USD 600.0 million of 6.00% senior unsecured notes due 2029 and an undrawn USD 350.0 million revolving facility maturing 2029-11-15; Purchasing Power receivables are funded by USD 272.0 million of non-recourse asset-backed notes; revolver security wording conflicts between reports
Recourse and non-recourse claims differ; asset-backed debt is 31.19% of principal debt
Originations, receivables and revenue peak in the fourth quarter
Year-end balance sheets carry the most lease merchandise and receivables

Investor Day targets of compound annual growth to 2028 on a pro forma 2025 basis: gross merchandise volume 20% to 25%, revenue 5% to 8%, adjusted EBITDA 13% to 16%, non-GAAP EPS 17% to 20% (management language)
Targets are management claims, not evidence

runs.text: Strengths, ranked by weight in the credit view:

- Low recourse leverage that was cut fast. The recourse claim is USD 600.0 million of notes and the company reports 1.5x net leverage after repaying USD 310.0 million of corporate borrowings within six months of the acquisition, which supports probability of default and recovery for the notes while that discipline lasts, although company-defined leverage is above the 1.08x of the end of 2025 because cash funded part of the acquisition. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 41; EX-99.3_2026-10-28_ex-993q32026earningssupp.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation C14; calculation C19; calculation C29

- Liquidity with no maturity before 2029. Cash of USD 108.9 million and an undrawn USD 350.0 million revolver total USD 458.9 million, no principal falls due until November 2029 and annual note interest is USD 36.0 million, so a near-term liquidity event would need a severe earnings collapse. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 41; calculation C15; calculation C18

- Capital-light cash generation. Capital expenditure is 0.59% of revenue and nine-month operating cash flow of USD 386.2 million funded debt repayment and distributions, which supports debt service, although part of it is a release of lease inventory. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C9; calculation C10; calculation C11

- Ring-fenced term funding for Purchasing Power receivables. USD 272.0 million of non-recourse asset-backed notes mature in 2030 at a weighted fixed coupon of 4.87% on the 2026 series and report no early amortization event, which keeps that funding off the corporate liquidity line while performance holds. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 40; calculation C17

- Short lease duration. Leases run up to 12 months and cancel at any time, so loss experience shows quickly and the company can tighten approvals within a quarter, as it did late in Q2 and again in Q3, which protects the portfolio at the cost of volume. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_prg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 55
Weaknesses, ranked by weight in the credit view:

- Earnings concentration in a shrinking core. Progressive Leasing produced 91.73% of nine-month pre-tax profit while its revenue fell 4.37%, so group debt service depends on the segment whose volume and write-offs are moving the wrong way. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 50; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 63; calculation C1; calculation C3

- Partner concentration. Customers of the top three partners produced 54.8% of 2025 revenue and two partners have failed since 2024, so a single partner event cuts volume with no contractual revenue floor because leases are cancellable. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_prg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 54

- Rising write-offs. Provisions reached 8.3% of Progressive Leasing revenue against 7.4%, above the 6% to 8% annual target, and each extra point costs about USD 22.45 million of EBITDA, so earnings are sensitive to consumer stress. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 63; calculation C20

- Revolver-funded shareholder returns. The announced USD 100.0 million repurchase uses cash and revolver borrowings and lifts reported net debt to EBITDA to 3.09x, while buybacks and dividends were 16.47% of nine-month operating cash flow, so distributions compete with deleveraging. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 72; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C13; calculation C19

- Unresolved covenant and refinancing position. The leverage covenant steps down from 3.25x to 3.00x in 2027 and 2.50x after on an unsupplied definition, and the notes and revolver both fall due in November 2029 with the notes estimated at 95.18% of par, so headroom and market access are not established. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39; calculation C16; calculation C27

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The only completed transaction that reshaped the group is the acquisition of Purchasing Power on January 2, 2026, made by a wholly owned subsidiary under a unit purchase agreement signed on December 1, 2025. Total consideration was USD 424.227 million in cash: USD 216.220 million to the seller, USD 199.283 million of seller debt settled at closing, USD 6.724 million of seller costs and USD 2.000 million of escrow, equal to a USD 420 million negotiated price plus USD 4.2 million of seller asset-backed debt repaid. USD 338.608 million of Purchasing Power non-recourse funding debt stayed in place, and net cash used after cash acquired was USD 391.8 million. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 27–31; 10-K_2025-12-31_prg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 157; calculation C7

New debt in 2026 was a Fourth Amendment to the credit facility that added a USD 125.0 million term loan, revolver borrowings of USD 185.0 million (USD 135.0 million for the acquisition and USD 50.0 million for working capital), and one new asset-backed issue: USD 220.0 million of Series 2026-A notes issued by a securitization entity on February 26, 2026 at coupons of 4.37% to 7.54%, maturing August 2030. No new corporate bonds were issued. About USD 224.0 million of assumed warehouse and securitization debt was repaid in February 2026, the revolver borrowings were repaid in Q1, and the term loan was prepaid in full by June 30, 2026, leaving the revolver undrawn at September 30, 2026. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 31–41; 10-K_2025-12-31_prg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 157; 10-Q_2026-03-31_prg-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-Q_2026-06-30_prg-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 38; calculation C16

After quarter end, the company announced on October 28, 2026 an intention to enter an accelerated share repurchase of about USD 100.0 million, to be funded with cash and revolver borrowings and completed across Q4 2026 and Q1 2027, and on October 26, 2026 the Board added USD 237.3 million to the repurchase authorization, restoring it to USD 500.0 million. This is an announced intention, not an executed transaction, and it is kept apart from the period figures. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prg-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 72; calculation C14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Governance risk is medium on behavior alone: PROG repaid its acquisition borrowings within six months, but it funded a USD 425.0 million tender offer with note proceeds in 2022 and has announced a USD 100.0 million accelerated share repurchase to be paid from cash and revolver borrowings, while board and ownership detail were not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Partner concentration is the main business risk and has already cost volume. Customers of the top three retail partners generated 54.8% of consolidated 2025 revenue and those of the top ten 77.0%, two partners each accounted for more than 10%, and two retail partners have failed since 2024 (Big Lots in September 2024 and American Signature in November 2025), so store closures cut Progressive Leasing volume and earnings independent of customer credit quality.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Credit performance at the core is weakening and management is trading volume for quality. Lease write-off provisions rose to 8.3% of Progressive Leasing revenue in Q3 2026 from 7.4%, above the top of the 6% to 8% annual target range, decisioning was tightened late in Q2 and again in Q3, and gross merchandise volume grew only 2.3% while revenue fell 0.7%, so tighter approvals protect losses at the cost of future revenue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Purchasing Power diversifies revenue but has not yet added profit. It supplied 16.88% of nine-month 2026 revenue but a pre-tax loss of USD 4.8 million, even after a USD 9.0 million fair-value gain on its receivables, and federal employee receivables, which employees may stop paying by allotment, are 9.80% of its post-acquisition accounts receivable with a past-due share of 17.35% against 12.25% for non-federal receivables.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The acquisition was funded with recourse debt that was repaid quickly, which is the clearest evidence in the documents of creditor-aligned policy. A USD 125.0 million term loan, a USD 135.0 million revolver draw and cash paid for the deal; revolver borrowings were repaid in Q1 and the term loan by June 30, 2026, and company-defined net leverage fell from about 2.5x after closing to 2.0x, 1.7x and 1.5x at the end of Q1, Q2 and Q3, at or inside the stated target range of 1.5x to 2.0x, although that measure excludes non-recourse asset-backed debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Shareholder returns have resumed, with one debt-funded precedent. A 2022 tender offer for USD 425.0 million was funded by note proceeds, repurchases resumed in Q2 2026 (USD 46.9 million in nine months) and the announced USD 100.0 million accelerated repurchase will use cash and revolver borrowings, but buybacks plus dividends were only 16.47% of nine-month 2026 operating cash flow, so deleveraging gains can be spent on equity if the revolver share is large.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Ownership and board evidence is thin, so governance conclusions rest on observed behavior and on the notes' summary of creditor protections. No controlling holder is identified in the supplied documents, the audited statements carry an unqualified opinion, and the notes carry a 101% change of control put and covenants on debt, liens, distributions and affiliate transactions, but board composition, ownership percentages and covenant baskets were not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a cautious reading is that diversification is real in growth and the new funding has performed as designed. Four grew nine-month pre-tax earnings by 359.5%, consolidated gross merchandise volume rose 58.9% in Q3, the asset-backed vehicles report covenant compliance and no early amortization event, and management says federal employee delinquencies have improved from the elevated 2025 level.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would soften if Progressive Leasing write-offs returned inside the 6% to 8% range while volume recovered, if Purchasing Power reached a sustained pre-tax profit without fair-value gains, or if the proxy statement and legal documents showed strong creditor protections. It would worsen if a top three partner left, if write-offs stayed above 8%, or if revolver-funded repurchases pushed company-defined net leverage above 2.0x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Partner names, contract terms and individual revenue shares are not supplied; only the top three and top ten shares and two unnamed partners above 10% are stated, so the concentration finding cannot be turned into an estimate of what the loss of one named partner would cost.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The proxy statement was not supplied, so board composition, control rights, executive pay and ownership percentages are not established and the medium governance rating rests on observed behavior; a controlling or activist holder would change it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The executed credit agreement, indenture and asset-backed documents were not supplied and the notes describe covenants without dollar baskets, so the legal room for new distributions or debt is not established and the behavior flags cannot be tied to a permitted amount.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Purchasing Power results before January 2, 2026 are available only in a pro forma note and the purchase price allocation is preliminary, so the finding that it adds revenue but not yet profit cannot be tested against its own history.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The only completed transaction that reshaped the group is the acquisition of Purchasing Power on January 2, 2026, made by a wholly owned subsidiary under a unit purchase agreement signed on December 1, 2025. Total consideration was USD 424.227 million in cash: USD 216.220 million to the seller, USD 199.283 million of seller debt settled at closing, USD 6.724 million of seller costs and USD 2.000 million of escrow, equal to a USD 420 million negotiated price plus USD 4.2 million of seller asset-backed debt repaid. USD 338.608 million of Purchasing Power non-recourse funding debt stayed in place, and net cash used after cash acquired was USD 391.8 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: New debt in 2026 was a Fourth Amendment to the credit facility that added a USD 125.0 million term loan, revolver borrowings of USD 185.0 million (USD 135.0 million for the acquisition and USD 50.0 million for working capital), and one new asset-backed issue: USD 220.0 million of Series 2026-A notes issued by a securitization entity on February 26, 2026 at coupons of 4.37% to 7.54%, maturing August 2030. No new corporate bonds were issued. About USD 224.0 million of assumed warehouse and securitization debt was repaid in February 2026, the revolver borrowings were repaid in Q1, and the term loan was prepaid in full by June 30, 2026, leaving the revolver undrawn at September 30, 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: After quarter end, the company announced on October 28, 2026 an intention to enter an accelerated share repurchase of about USD 100.0 million, to be funded with cash and revolver borrowings and completed across Q4 2026 and Q1 2027, and on October 26, 2026 the Board added USD 237.3 million to the repurchase authorization, restoring it to USD 500.0 million. This is an announced intention, not an executed transaction, and it is kept apart from the period figures.

Countervailing evidence is the rapid repayment of the acquisition debt, company net leverage of 1.5x and the noteholders' 101% change of control put. Further analysis requires the proxy statement, the credit agreement and the indenture. The governance view is complete with limitations, and the key gaps are the proxy statement, the legal documents and partner-level concentration detail.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: PROG is a financial technology holding company whose profit comes mostly from one business. Progressive Leasing leases durable goods to near-prime and subprime consumers through about 24,000 partner locations and websites, and generated 91.73% of nine-month 2026 pre-tax profit and 77.70% of revenue. Purchasing Power, acquired on 2026-01-02, sells goods to employees of employer clients through payroll deduction, and Four offers buy now pay later; with the small Other segment they supplied the remaining 22.30% of revenue. Leases run for a fixed term of up to 12 months and the customer may cancel at any time by returning the merchandise, so revenue visibility is about one lease term and earnings follow approvals and partner volume quickly in both directions. The working asset is lease merchandise of USD 511.293 million and capital expenditure is only 0.59% of revenue, so cash generation depends on keeping approvals, losses and partner volume stable; that supports debt service while volume is steady and weakens it quickly when it is not.

fields.value: Progressive Leasing revenue is recurring within each lease term but discretionary, cyclical and concentrated. Volume grew 1.20% in nine months and 2.3% in Q3 on a larger e-commerce share, yet revenue fell 4.37% over nine months and 0.69% in Q3 because smaller lease portfolios entered each period; active customers were flat at 781 thousand against 784 thousand. Customers of the top three partners produced 54.8% of 2025 revenue (USD 1,320.3 million) and the top ten 77.0%, partner contracts can be renegotiated or not renewed, and two retail partners have failed since 2024, so a partner event is a step-down in volume rather than a gradual drift. Management attributes the pressure to cost of living, fuel prices and the war in Iran, expects tighter decisioning to keep pressuring volume, and has reduced its 2026 revenue and earnings outlook ranges. Purchasing Power and Four are growing but small: consolidated revenue ex Purchasing Power fell 0.86% in nine months, so the group's growth is acquired.

Free cash flow after capital expenditure was USD 324.9 million in FY2025 and USD 373.1 million in nine months of 2026, and USD 309.5 million after buybacks and dividends. The USD 310.0 million of corporate borrowings was repaid and corporate debt is back to the USD 600.0 million of notes, but cash fell from USD 308.774 million to USD 108.917 million, so net recourse debt rose by USD 199.857 million over nine months; conversion of this size is not durable, because a volume recovery would absorb cash in inventory again.

fields.value: Competitive rivalry is high: the annual report describes the virtual lease-to-own market as highly competitive with new payment products, and Four competes with other buy now pay later providers, cards and digital wallets, so pricing power is limited and approvals, not price, are the lever management uses. Buyer power sits with the large retail partners, who can renegotiate rebates, exclusivity and merchandise prices; incentive payments were USD 25.2 million in nine months, so any worse terms reduce margin directly. Substitutes are plentiful for the same customer, which limits pricing power. Entrants matter less than partner concentration. Of the macro and policy factors only two change the credit view. Economic: inflation, fuel prices, tariffs and unemployment fall on near-prime and subprime customers first and show up in write-offs within a lease term. Regulatory: state attorneys general have acted against rent-to-own disclosure, a state demand arrived in October 2026, and seven states opened a coordinated inquiry into buy now pay later providers that did not name Four, so enforcement is a recurring cost and practice risk to the core segment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: In credit terms the strengths are low recourse debt, short lease duration, low capital intensity, liquidity with no maturity until 2029 and fixed-rate term funding for the new receivables; the weaknesses are earnings concentration in one segment, partner concentration, rising write-offs, revolver-funded shareholder returns and an unresolved covenant measure. The opportunities that could improve credit quality are Four's profit growth and a Purchasing Power move to profit; the threats that could weaken it are a top three partner exit, a consumer downturn and enforcement outcomes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Scale is adequate for a niche consumer payments issuer, but the competitive position rests on partner relationships rather than a moat, and diversification is improving only in revenue. Cost and capex flexibility is good because merchandise cost and capital spending move with volume, margin stability is average because write-offs are rising, and free cash flow stability is average because conversion swung between 62.66% and 145.13% of EBITDA. Access to capital markets is adequate: the notes are priced at 95.18% of par on an estimated basis and the asset-backed notes were placed in February 2026, but no ratings were supplied. Liquidity is strong against dated obligations at USD 458.9 million, and financial policy is average because deleveraging was fast while distributions resumed. Trend: reported net leverage moved from 2.50x to 1.24x to 2.73x, and interest cover on reported EBITDA from 5.97x to 6.17x to 5.06x, so the profile is weaker than at the end of 2025 on leverage, interest cover and liquidity, although EBITDA is higher; variable-rate debt is small, a one percentage point rate change moves annual interest by about USD 0.5 million, and no hedges are used. Key missing datapoints are the covenant definitions, the adjusted EBITDA reconciliation and the credit agreement terms.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over 12 to 24 months the central case is flat to lower Progressive Leasing earnings with tighter approvals, stable leverage on the company definition and an accelerated repurchase that raises reported leverage. Headwinds are the cost of living and fuel prices that management cites, partner closures that continue through 2026, the tightened decisioning that management expects to pressure volume, a reduced 2026 outlook, and the covenant step-down to 3.00x in 2027; tailwinds are e-commerce growth at 26.4% of volume, improving federal employee delinquencies at Purchasing Power, Four's profit growth and the integration of Purchasing Power into one system by early 2027. Over three to five years management's growth targets to 2028 are claims, not evidence, and the more important dated event is the refinancing of the notes and revolver in November 2029, when the notes become current a year earlier.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The initiating condition is a further consumer shock from fuel prices and unemployment, or the loss of another large retail partner. The first operational break is at Progressive Leasing: delinquencies rise, write-offs move above 8% of revenue and approvals tighten again, so volume falls and lease revenue follows with a lag of a lease term, as it already did in Q3 when volume grew and revenue did not. Financially, one extra point of write-offs on last-twelve-months Progressive Leasing revenue costs USD 22.45 million, 8.10% of reported EBITDA, and a 5% fall in that revenue at the Q3 gross margin removes USD 35.70 million of gross margin, 12.88% of reported EBITDA, before any cost response. Cash is cushioned first because a shrinking lease book releases inventory cash, which hides the earnings fall for several quarters, then the cushion fades as purchases fall with volume. On the reported basis a one point rise in write-offs lifts net debt to EBITDA from 2.73x to 2.97x, and to 3.36x with the full repurchase; on the company definition the same two events give 1.99x, at the top of the 1.5x to 2.0x range, and cover on reported EBITDA falls to 4.65x. Liquidity of USD 458.9 million, no maturity before 2029 and USD 36.0 million of annual note interest mean distress is unlikely within 12 to 24 months; management levers are to cancel the repurchase, cut lease merchandise purchases, sell charged-off receivables and cut costs. The observable triggers are write-offs above 8% for a second quarter, a partner exit, a revolver draw, a rising notes discount and any change in covenant compliance language.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, PROG Holdings presents an adequate business profile supported by short-duration leases, low capital intensity, a recourse structure limited to USD 600.0 million of notes and liquidity of USD 458.9 million, but credit quality is constrained by a shrinking and concentrated core earnings engine, rising write-offs and shareholder returns that are partly revolver funded. No peer data were supplied, so the profile cannot be benchmarked against typical leveraged consumer finance issuers. Cash-flow durability appears adequate rather than strong because recent conversion was helped by inventory release and a tax refund. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on Progressive Leasing earnings holding up until the notes and revolver mature in November 2029, on the covenant definition and on whether the repurchase is revolver funded. The primary downside path is partner loss or rising write-offs at Progressive Leasing feeding through to leverage while distributions continue. Further analysis would require the credit agreement and covenant definitions, the adjusted EBITDA reconciliation, partner-level concentration and the proxy statement. Top risk: erosion of Progressive Leasing earnings through partner loss or rising write-offs.
